author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: Staff open a read-only specialty directory, reached by its address alone, that lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it, each shown by full name, all on one unpaged page. A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on it.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
Each veterinarian on the specialty directory is shown by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on the specialty directory.
Every specialty is listed on the one page, with no paging, whatever the number of specialties.
Edge case 3: a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed under each of them.
Edge case 4: a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, and is shown as held by none rather than left blank.
Edge case 5: specialties appear in alphabetical order of name; the veterinarians under each appear in order of last name, then first name.
The specialty directory carries the navigation every page carries, to owner search and to the veterinarian directory (REQ-SYS-001).
No page, and no navigation entry, links to the specialty directory; it is reachable by its address alone.
Every piece of wording the page adds is present in every supported language and none is hard-coded (REQ-LANG-002); specialty and veterinarian names appear as stored, untranslated.
non_goals: Adding, changing, or removing a veterinarian, a specialty, or who holds which: NG-2 is unchanged (intake line 1 decision).
A navigation entry for the specialty directory, or a link to it from any other page: the owner deferred a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request (intake line 1 decision).
Searching or filtering veterinarians by specialty, or a separate page per specialty: NG-9 declines veterinarian search, and the request lists every specialty on one page.
A machine-readable form of the specialty directory: the request names one HTML page, and REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn for the same shape on the veterinarian list.
Paging the specialty directory: the request states no pagination.
Any change to the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001).
Translating specialty names: the request shows each by its stored name.
notes: Owner decisions quoted verbatim in intake-decision line 1: read-only specialty view in scope with NG-2 unchanged; page reachable by URL alone. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. The owner asked for the narrowest reading plus recorded open questions, so two reversible presentation choices were made and recorded as PRD edge cases 4-5, pending confirmation under Open Questions. First, a specialty nobody holds is shown as held by none, mirroring REQ-VET-001. Second, the page uses alphabetical order. A visible entry point stays open and deferred, and this slice does not need it. The seed data exercises the criteria: James Carter and Sharon Jenkins hold no specialty, and Linda Douglas holds two. Autofix audit: the log had no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory stays inside the vet package and uses three In-force catalog patterns (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). (1) A new read-only SpecialtyRepository extends the Spring Data Repository marker. It follows VetRepository's form, declares one transactional read-only findAll() and no write method, and is uncached. It is needed because edge case 4 lists specialties nobody holds, which cannot be derived from veterinarians alone. (2) A new immutable value object, SpecialtyDirectory, built from every specialty plus every veterinarian. It carries only strings: each specialty's stored name in alphabetical order, with the full names ('First Last') of its holders, ordered by last name then first name. It matches holders to specialties by identifier, never by instance. It leaves out veterinarians holding no specialty, lists a veterinarian under each specialty held, and keeps an unheld specialty with an empty holder list. (3) A new GET /specialties.html handler on VetController. It reads VetRepository.findAll() (existing, cached) and SpecialtyRepository.findAll(), builds SpecialtyDirectory, adds it to the model, and returns vets/specialtyList. The new template, templates/vets/specialtyList.html, uses the shared layout fragment; its only wording is #{...} keys, and an empty holder list renders #{none}. Durable-memory writes: Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory; REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty, VetRepository and VetController rows; one invariant line recording that BaseEntity defines no equality; the provenance banner noting REQ-VET-003 as designed rather than derived; the vet package line in Package Structure. No ADR: every choice sits inside the In-force catalog and departs from nothing.
integration_points: Binding, GET /specialties.html: the handler binds no request input (no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @ModelAttribute or form object), so it has no binding target and needs no @InitBinder. Adding any request parameter later is a design change that needs a new triage (security-principles § Realization, mass-assignment row).

Double, SpecialtyDirectoryTests (unit, no boundary crossed): real Vet and Specialty instances built through setters. The persistence-entity exception covers their mutability (architecture-principles § Scoped exception). Build distinct Specialty instances that share an id to exercise identifier matching. No mock of any kind (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, real objects first).
Double, VetControllerTests framework transport: MockMvc through the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class), the one sanctioned mock (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Double, VetControllerTests VetRepository boundary: keep the existing @MockitoBean. It is a tolerated pre-existing stub, and its @BeforeEach findAll() stub already supplies James Carter (no specialty) and Helen Leary (radiology id 1). Add no new Mockito stubbing for the new tests beyond reusing it.

Double, VetControllerTests SpecialtyRepository boundary: a hand-written double, not a @MockitoBean. Use a nested static @TestConfiguration exposing a SpecialtyRepository bean as a lambda over its single findAll() method. It returns a fixed list: radiology as a distinct instance with id 1, plus one specialty nobody holds. The bean also satisfies the new VetController constructor argument for the existing tests (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, hand-write mocks).

Real I/O, PetClinicIntegrationTests: add one GET /specialties.html check against the H2 seed data through the running server. It is the only test where the cached veterinarians and the freshly loaded specialties come from different persistence contexts, so it proves identifier matching end to end. Seed facts: Carter and Jenkins hold nothing; Douglas holds surgery and dentistry.

Navigation: specialtyList.html passes the layout fragment a menu value that matches no nav entry, so no entry reads as active. layout.html and every other template stay unchanged: no link to /specialties.html anywhere (PRD REQ-VET-003 acceptance criteria).

Message bundles: every key the page adds goes into all eleven messages*.properties files. Reuse the existing specialties, vets, name and none keys where their wording fits. Specialty and veterinarian names render through th:text untranslated (PRD REQ-LANG-002; system-design § Contracts, the paragraph on REQ-LANG-002).

patterns.description: Read-only repository form to copy for SpecialtyRepository: extend the Repository marker, add @Transactional(readOnly = true) on findAll(), expose no write method. Do not copy PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository base, which exposes writes that NG-2 rules out.
Natural String order on NamedEntity::getName: SpecialtyDirectory orders specialty names the same way (architecture-principles § Design Principles, consistency over novelty).
HTML handler shape: GET mapping, Model attribute, view name under vets/. The new handler holds no rule and delegates the shaping to SpecialtyDirectory.
Layout fragment inclusion, th:text rendering, and the #{none} fallback for an empty specialty set, mirrored for an empty holder list.

risks.risk: Grouping holders by Specialty instance silently empties every specialty. BaseEntity defines no equals, and the cached veterinarians' specialties are different instances from the freshly loaded ones.
risks.mitigation: Match by getId() (system-design § Contracts, invariants paragraph). Unit tests use distinct instances sharing an id; the web double and the integration check exercise the same split.

risks.risk: Putting the exclusion, grouping, held-by-none or ordering logic in VetController would be a fresh Web-controller violation and widen the pyramid gap.
risks.mitigation: All four live in SpecialtyDirectory and are unit-tested without the framework; the handler only reads, constructs and selects the view (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and the paragraph after it; testing-principles § Test Pyramid).

risks.risk: A value object that holds Vet or Specialty references inherits their mutability, and the persistence-entity exception does not cover non-framework types.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory holds only strings in unmodifiable lists (List.copyOf) with value equality (architecture-principles § Domain Core, closed properties; § Scoped exception, Does-not-cover row).

risks.risk: Relying on database ORDER BY makes the order vendor-dependent, since collation and case handling differ across H2, MySQL and PostgreSQL.
risks.mitigation: Order in Java inside SpecialtyDirectory; the repository makes no ordering promise (system-design § Persistence; Known Defects, PostgreSQL case-sensitivity row).

risks.risk: Thymeleaf reads SpecialtyDirectory reflectively, and a native image has no reflection hint for the new types. The gate's JVM build cannot see this.
risks.mitigation: Register reflection hints for SpecialtyDirectory and its nested element type, either with @RegisterReflectionForBinding on the handler or in PetClinicRuntimeHints (system-design § Overview, native-image support).

risks.risk: The page is unpaged and unbounded, and holders come from the uncached-eviction 'vets' cache while specialties are read fresh, so an out-of-band change can show a mixed view.
risks.mitigation: Accepted. Specialties are a clinic-maintained lookup list with no write path (PRD NG-2), and findAll() already loads every veterinarian for the serialized route (system-design § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5). Add no cache and no limit.

risks.risk: The new endpoint widens the exposed surface.
risks.mitigation: It exposes, to any caller, only the veterinarian and specialty names /vets.html already exposes. It is read-only GET with no request-derived input reaching a query or resource path, and output escaping stays on through th:text, never th:utext (security-principles § Realization, widening-surface and cross-site-scripting rows).

notes: Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records. Test placement: ordering, exclusion, listing under each specialty held, the empty holder list for an unheld specialty, and 'every specialty, whatever the count' are rules below the boundary, so they belong in SpecialtyDirectoryTests (testing-principles § Test Pyramid). VetControllerTests keeps the rendered acceptance: every specialty with holders, 'Helen Leary' first-then-last, the #{none} wording, no paging controls, the shared navigation, and no navigation entry for /specialties.html. The implementer maps the prd-entry test_names across the two classes on that split. SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyRepository stay package-private unless the template engine cannot read a package-private type; that engine is the named caller that would justify widening (architecture-principles § Design Principles, minimal surface). Presentation choices from PRD edge cases 4 and 5 are reversible and pending owner confirmation; the design isolates both in SpecialtyDirectory.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: New route GET /specialties.html (VetController.java `public String showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model)`) binds no request input: no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody on it. The only request binding in the vet package is the pre-existing `showVetList(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page, Model model)` at VetController.java:49 (grep -F for save/@PostMapping/@RequestParam/@ModelAttribute/@PathVariable over src/main/java/.../vet/). There is no mass-assignment, injection or path-selection surface, and the view name is the fixed literal "vets/specialtyList".

Least privilege on data access: SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> and declares only `@Transactional(readOnly = true) Collection<Specialty> findAll()`. It exposes no write method and no custom or concatenated query. The same grep finds no `save` anywhere in the vet package, so no request can add vets or specialties. The unpaged findAll over both tables required by the PRD therefore stays bounded by operator-seeded reference data, the same reach the pre-existing unpaged GET /vets already has.

XSS: specialtyList.html renders stored values only through escaped `th:text` (`${listing.specialtyName}`, `${holders.last ? holderName : holderName + ', '}`) and message keys. It adds no th:utext and no `__${...}__` preprocessing: a grep -F for `utext` and `__${` over src/main/resources/templates/ matches only the pre-existing layout, fragment, vetList and owner templates, not the new file. The layout menu argument is the constant 'specialties', so no new href is built from data.

Surface widening is stated and minimal: the PRD and system-design rows describe the page as read-only and reached only by its address, and VetControllerTests asserts no navigation link to it. It exposes names that GET /vets.html and GET /vets already publish, and no new management or actuator exposure.

Concurrency: SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable record with List.copyOf in both canonical constructors and holds no entity references. It only reads the shared @Cacheable("vets") Vet instances through Vet.getSpecialties(), which returns a fresh sorted copy (Vet.java `.sorted(Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName)).collect(Collectors.toList())`). The singleton controller holds only final repository fields.

The single @RegisterReflectionForBinding(SpecialtyDirectory.class) native-image hint registers a package-private read-only record for template reflection. It enables no Java serialization and no deserialization entry point.

No secrets, credentials, logging, file I/O, process execution or Jackson polymorphic typing in the diff (read of the full unified diff from scripts/changeset.sh). No change to build.gradle, pom.xml, gradle/ or application properties (`git diff --stat` on those paths is empty).

Supply chain: no dependency change. OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured in build.gradle (grep -F for dependencyCheck/owasp found nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5, tools.jackson.core jackson-databind 3.1.5. ./gradlew test was not run by this reviewer; the build-pass at line 7 records the gate.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Additive change confined to the vet package: a new read-only repository, an immutable value object, one new GET handler, and a new template. The existing /vets.html and /vets routes are untouched, and the only changed existing signature is the VetController constructor, which only VetControllerTests wires. The security-surface flag on VetController is a no-input GET that returns a fixed view name, and no sensitive paths are touched.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk. Holders are matched by specialty id, never by instance, which is correct because BaseEntity defines no equals and the cached vets hold different instances. Ordering is done in Java with the same case-sensitive natural order Vet.getSpecialties uses. Reading the cached Vet entities mutates nothing, since getSpecialties returns a sorted copy. The template renders only through escaped th:text, and the menu value 'specialties' matches no nav item, so no entry appears.

test_adequacy.note: Unit tests compare whole objects and cover the rules that could break: distinct instances sharing an id, the same-last-name tiebreak (Anna before Helen Leary), exclusion of vets holding nothing, and an unheld specialty kept with no holders. An integration test on seeded H2 data checks id matching across persistence contexts end to end. The jacoco report shows 0 missed lines for SpecialtyDirectory, Listing and VetController. The controller-level no-paging check is thin (it only asserts no page= link), but the unit count test covers that rule.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved with no findings and no recommendations, and the unconfigured OWASP scanner is a standing gap, not a hedge. Most citations check out (VetController.java:49 and :71-77, prd.md:179, system-design.md:36 and :104-105). One does not: code-quality-reviewer reports a grep matching 'extends Repository' at VetRepository.java:44, but that grep finds it at line 38. Line 44 is the @Transactional line the design-block cited, so the reported grep output was not real. The underlying claim is true: I confirmed VetRepository extends the Repository marker.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations or build retries. Every touched path is in the design-block's primary or supporting paths. Existing message keys were reused, and all ten bundles already carry them. The native-image hint uses the annotation option the design allowed. layout.html is unchanged, so no navigation entry was added, and the doc edits match the design-block's declared memory writes.

rationale: The code and tests read clean and stay within the triaged scope. The one flag is evidence quality: code-quality-reviewer reported a grep line number the grep cannot produce, which weakens that approval. Before merging, spend a short read on SpecialtyRepository and the new VetController handler, the parts that approval covered. I found the substance correct.
